claims.head: Expect the Penguins to have the puck more
claims.body: At 5-on-5, the Penguins have been near the top of the league at getting more of the chances than they give up, and the Predators near the bottom. The ice should tilt the Penguins’ way, even if goaltending and bounces have the final say on the score.

claims.head: The Penguins hunt better looks than the Predators
claims.body: The Penguins wait for good looks, but the Predators settle for hopeful ones. Pittsburgh is one of the league’s best for shot quality, and Nashville is near the bottom. The more dangerous chances should be the Penguins’.

notes.text: The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 9 games cover only 33% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the 9th-lowest in the league (a typical team: 43%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.
Spencer Stastney is no longer killing penalties: 5% of the team’s shorthanded time in 6 games, down from 31% with his old team last season.

items.text: The Penguins are newly without Ben Kindel, Egor Chinakhov and Evgeni Malkin, and have been without Trevor van Riemsdyk since Oct 9.
Steven Stamkos has five goals in seven games against Pittsburgh since 2023-24.
Nick Perbix has missed the Predators’ latest game.
With Ben Kindel out, Connor Dewar took nine faceoffs in the Penguins’ last game. He had been taking about one a game.
